nodes.rationale: compose(f, g) builds a new function equivalent to calling g first and passing its result to f, letting complex behavior be built from small, independently-testable pieces instead of one large function.

nodes.label: Partial Application

nodes.label: Pure Functions

nodes.label: Category parity across language tracks
nodes.rationale: Category parity across languages is a choice, not an enforced rule. Python/Java share the same 14 category keys; C++ ships its own smaller 6-category set; Spring goes furthest with only 3 categories (dependency_injection, bean_lifecycle, configuration_profiles) with no equivalent at all in the other tracks, since categories like packaging/deployment/observability are ecosystem/tooling concepts that fit a package manager or framework better than bare language or DI-framework content. Nothing in ExerciseEngine.categories() hardcodes which categories a language 'should' have -- it's derived purely from what's present in that language's content directory, so a different-sized category set required zero app-code changes.

nodes.label: Real-toolchain verification step
nodes.rationale: The most important step when adding language content, and has caught real bugs every time it's been skipped: write the fixed solution, run it through the real engine (not a guess at output), assert success/output/contains_patterns match, and separately confirm the unedited starter code does NOT silently pass validation. Toolchain crash/error messages should be verified against actual observed stderr, not assumed.

nodes.label: importlib.metadata
nodes.rationale: importlib.metadata.version() reads installed package metadata without importing the package, enabling feature-detection; it raises PackageNotFoundError for missing packages, which callers should catch rather than crash on.

nodes.label: Lock Files
nodes.rationale: A lock file records the exact version actually installed rather than an acceptable range, so re-installing later or on another machine resolves to the identical version; a resolver that ignores the pin defeats that reproducibility guarantee.

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: requirements.txt pins have a simple, predictable 'name==version' shape that can be parsed with str.partition on the first '==' rather than pulling in a full parser dependency.

nodes.label: Versioning
nodes.rationale: Version strings must be split into numeric components and compared as tuples of ints; plain string comparison is lexicographic and gets multi-digit segments (e.g. '10' vs '9') wrong.

nodes.label: Virtual Environments
nodes.rationale: sys.prefix differs from sys.base_prefix exactly when a virtualenv is active; comparing them is the standard, dependency-free venv-detection check used internally by pip and other tools.
